title: Brentford vs. Chelsea: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 16, 2026The hosts have seen 13 goals scored in their six games this season—the visitors a huge 28.  / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Everton’s badge), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Chelsea’s badge) Chelsea make the trip up to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton in Saturday’s early Premier League kickoff.

Despite a wretched end to their summer transfer window, leaving themselves short in attack and at fullback, the Toffees are a game away from enjoying their longest unbeaten run to start a Premier League season since 2006–07. David Moyes‘s side slumped toward the finish line last season, meaning they missed out on European soccer. Still, they’ve returned with a rejuvenated presence at the start of the new campaign.
A 10-point haul leaves them fifth in the table at this early juncture, and they’re only ahead of their upcoming opponents on goal difference.

Chelsea’s sole blemish was a 3–0 defeat at Brentford before the international break, when Xabi Alonso was without an array of stars for a tricky away encounter. The Blues responded last weekend by producing what the manager described as a “complete performance” to thrash Bournemouth 5–1.
While plenty have scrutinized the start of Alonso’s reign, Chelsea are in a pretty good place and will eventually benefit from their free midweeks.

João Pedro is in superb form. / Steffan Bowen/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesChelsea’s first trip to Everton’s new home returned a 3–0 defeat. Robert Sánchez had a nightmare between the posts, as the energetic Toffees bullied a team briefly managed by Liam Rosenior.

Early kickoffs can often be dreary affairs, benefiting the away side. The Blues have struggled on their days out to the blue half of Merseyside in recent years, winning on just one of their previous nine visits. The bulk of these woes came at Goodison Park, yet their defeat here in March suggested it wasn’t merely Everton’s classic amphitheatre that was the issue. It’s something in the air.
Perhaps this time things will be different.

Everton should have Vitalii Mykolenko back in action. /   Moyes offered a "much better injury update" ahead of Chelsea’s visit, with Everton potentially having starting left back Vitalii Mykolenko available for the game.

Mykolenko missed last week’s draw at Hull due to a knock he sustained while playing for Ukraine during the recent break, forcing Jarrad Branthwaite into a wide position as cover. While Moyes must decide whether to take a chance on Mykolenko’s fitness or take a cautious stance given the lack of alternatives, Everton are pretty settled elsewhere.

Thierno Barry missed a bucketload but did get his goal at Hull last weekend, and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is building on an excellent debut season with the Toffees. The midfielder, who lines up against his former club here, scored and assisted in Everton’s 2–2 draw.
Everton predicted lineup vs. Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry.

Chelsea could be unchanged from last week’s beatdown of Bournemouth. /   There’s every chance Alonso names an unchanged team for Satuarday’s trip to Merseyside, given how well Chelsea performed against Bournemouth last week.

Moisés Caicedo’s return to the Blues’ midfield proved imperative, and the Ecuadorian will likely be partnered by Jordan Henderson again after he struck twice against the Cherries. While Alonso has Roméo Lavia to call upon, captain Reece James has undergone knee surgery that’s set to sideline him for months.

Summer arrival Marco Palestra made his Premier League bow last weekend, and he’ll be pushing fellow newbie Pep Chavarría for a starting role before the November international break. Young defender Josh Acheampong replaced Wesley Fofana last time out, and there’s no reason for Alonso to make another change.
Emmanuel Emegha remains sidelined for the visitors, and Jamie Gittens will spend a few weeks on the sidelines after picking up an injury on international duty.
Chelsea predicted lineup vs. Everton (3-4-2-1): Martínez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Henderson, Caicedo, Chavarría; Palmer, Rogers; Pedro.
